title: The wisdom of Eli Dourado - Marginal REVOLUTION
gist: Drawing on direct experience as a State Department advisor in treaty negotiations and UN technical committees, the quoted argument is that 'international efforts' cannot solve AI governance because treaty processes are systematically hijacked as leverage for unrelated agendas, no major country binds itself meaningfully, and delegations are captured by the very industry interests they would regulate.

insights.claim: Every treaty or international agreement becomes an opportunity for participants to manipulate the broader policy environment, with negotiators often indifferent to the agreement's stated object and instead using it as leverage for something else entirely.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Treat announced international AI or tech accords as bargaining chips in unrelated disputes rather than as binding constraints when pricing regulatory risk.
insights.quote: Every single treaty or international agreement is an opportunity for every participant to manipulate the much broader policy environment.
insights.locator: The international sector is unbelievably dysfunctional

insights.claim: Countries have used their limited leverage in multilateral agreements to try to kneecap American industry, get around sanctions, create a pretense of international justification for domestic illiberalism, or steer technology in an authoritarian direction.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Multilateral tech rulemaking is an attack surface on US industrial competitiveness and sanctions enforcement — read proposed international standards as competitive weapons.
insights.quote: I have seen countries use their limited leverage in multilateral agreements to try to kneecap American industry, get around sanctions, create a pretense of international justification for domestic illiberalism, or steer technology in an authoritarian direction.
insights.locator: Often the participants don’t care about the object

insights.claim: The damage from dysfunctional treaty-making is contained because essentially no major country will actually bind itself in meaningful ways it does not narrowly want, and inconvenient signed treaties are often subtly ignored or reinterpreted.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Treaty headlines rarely change real capital allocation; the enforcement-free equilibrium means domestic policy and export controls remain the binding constraints.
insights.quote: If a previously signed treaty turns out to be inconvenient, it is often subtly ignored or reinterpreted.
insights.locator: The damage from this dysfunction is limited

insights.claim: Treaty delegations on industrial issues embed the full spectrum of special interests — a US AI treaty delegation led by a State Department ambassador would be advised by the interagency, major AI labs, other major tech companies, tech investors and civil society — so the negotiating position is captured before talks begin.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Any international AI regime will encode incumbent lab preferences; expect rules that raise compliance barriers for challengers rather than constrain the leaders.
insights.quote: A US AI treaty delegation might be led by a State Department ambassador, but he will be advised by representatives of the interagency, major labs, other major tech companies, tech investors, civil society, etc.
insights.locator: In addition, treaty delegations working on industrial issues

insights.claim: Invoking 'international efforts' as the answer to the AI governance problem simply relabels the problem, because the international sector is itself an enormous, unresolved governance problem.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Cuts against the consensus that coordinated global AI rules are the safe default — an argument that national-level policy and unilateral compute controls remain the only operative levers.
insights.quote: “International efforts,” therefore, is not a reassuring answer to the governance problem; it is the name of another enormous, unresolved governance problem.
insights.locator: “International efforts,” therefore, is not a reassuring answer
